svg.title: Direct Lake Query Path vs DirectQuery Fallback
svg.desc: A flow diagram starting from a report visual issuing a query. The query reaches the semantic model, which checks whether requested columns are already resident in memory; if not, it loads them lazily from OneLake anchored to the most recent framing operation. For Direct Lake on SQL models, three documented triggers (SQL views, SQL RLS, or capacity guardrails) branch into DirectQuery fallback against the SQL analytics endpoint.
svg.text: Direct Lake Query Execution Path vs Fallback
Visual DAX Request ➔ In-Memory VertiPaq Cache ➔ Lazy OneLake Load & Framing ➔ SQL Fallback Triggers
PHASE 1: THE DIRECT LAKE FAST PATH (ZERO SQL OVERHEAD · SUB-SECOND DAX)

g.title: Report visual issues a query — A Power BI visual requests data, consumed exactly like any other semantic model.
g.text: Identical behavior for Excel, DAX & Visuals

g.title: Column residency check — The engine checks whether requested columns are already resident in an in-memory cache.
g.text: • Eviction triggered only under RAM cap
Direct Lake RAM Limit per Model:

g.title: Lazy load from OneLake — Non-resident columns load directly from the OneLake Delta table, anchored to the last framing point.
g.text: • No data copy or model refresh job
• Data stays anchored to active frame
Direct Lake on OneLake skips SQL RLS

g.title: Framing (point-in-time anchor) — A metadata-only refresh that rebinds the model to the current Delta commit version, usually in seconds.

svg.text: PHASE 2: DIRECT LAKE ON SQL — DIRECTQUERY FALLBACK DECISION TREE & TRAPS

g.aria-label: DirectQuery fallback trigger check (SQL flavor only)
g.title: DirectQuery fallback trigger check (SQL flavor only) — Direct Lake on SQL checks three documented conditions that force a fallback to DirectQuery.
g.text: Direct Lake on SQL: Fallback Trigger Evaluation
DirectLakeBehavior property controls routing when conditions trip
Flavor Distinction: Direct Lake on OneLake vs on SQL
• Direct Lake on OneLake: NEVER falls back to DirectQuery. Skips SQL endpoint entirely.
• Direct Lake on SQL: Evaluates the 3 documented fallback conditions below:
SQL-Endpoint View Used as Table Source
• Direct Lake requires physical Delta Parquet files in OneLake.
• Views lack physical storage ➔ 100% of queries against view fall back to DirectQuery.
• Security predicate cannot be evaluated during binary OneLake columnar load.
• DAX query must route to SQL Engine to enforce SQL security context.
Table File Count Exceeds Capacity Guardrail
• Delta table accumulates > 10,000 uncompacted Parquet files.
• Framing metadata overhead breaches limit ➔ routes to SQL endpoint fallback.
Automatic (Fallback Allowed) · DirectLakeOnly (Hard Failure on Trigger Trip)

g.title: DirectQuery fallback — Query reads the SQL analytics endpoint live, escaping the framing snapshot at the cost of speed.
g.text: Visual DAX converted to relational SQL query
Distributed query executed by SQL engine
Escapes framing snapshot; fresh data returned
❌ Draws heavy interactive CU on capacity
✓ Returns absolute live state from lakehouse
✓ Fully respects SQL view logic & SQL RLS
Check DAX Studio / SQL Profiler DirectQuery Events

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL views force permanent fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL views force permanent fallback — Basing a Direct Lake on SQL table on a view sends every query into DirectQuery fallback, invisibly.
g.text: • No error or warning is shown in UI
• 100% of queries quietly route to SQL DQ
Result: Direct Lake speed is lost entirely!
Point semantic model tables directly to
physical lakehouse Delta tables on OneLake.
Run Spark or Data Factory pipelines to
If you need Direct Lake performance,
NEVER build models over SQL Views.
